title: Till Prospero breaks his staff, buries it certain fathoms in the earth and drowns his book
html_source:
The Tempest, Act V, Scene 1, Prospero says:

I’ll break my staff,
Bury it certain fathoms in the earth,
And deeper than did ever plummet sound
I’ll drown my book.

Believed by some to be Shakespeare’s last play.

Some also believe that the character of Prospero is something of a self-portrait and that Prospero’s destroying of his implements of magic is a metaphor for Shakespeare abandoning his creative endeavors.

In the play, Prospero is a Duke whose office had been usurped by his brother. Prospero had then been banished.
